comments.body: Claude slice landed (2026-10-13): an `approval` config asset in `assets/approvals/<name>.md`, using render.rad's Markdown grammar (`## <kind> [target...]: <title>`). Entries install as owned elements of Claude's autoMode.environment / allow / soft_deny arrays at user scope; an array tai creates is seeded with "$defaults". Still open: the Codex half (auto_review.extra_policy in config.toml, codex features list validation and rollback), and migrating tai-personal's auto-approval bundle off render.rad (another repo; drop the Claude profile's post_install step there, keep the Codex one until the Codex slice lands).
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Claude Code's auto-mode classifier and Codex's auto-review both read a standing approval policy written as prose, and tai has no asset for it. On Claude Code the policy is the `autoMode.environment`, `autoMode.allow` and `autoMode.soft_deny` arrays in `settings.json`; on Codex it is the `auto_review.extra_policy` Markdown string in `config.toml`.

Today the policy ships as file assets (one Markdown file per entry) plus a `render.rad` script that every profile's `post_install` runs (`assets/files/auto-approval/render.rad` in the tai-personal repo). `render.rad` owns the whole arrays and the whole `[auto_review]` table, so it overwrites entries set by hand, where tai's own config assets (hooks, MCP servers) own only the entries they wrote. It is also the main reason post_install steps carry real work (cards `run-post-install-as` and `let-a-bundle-declare`).

Proposed: an approval-policy config asset whose entries have a kind (context, allow, deny) and optional per-target scoping.

- Claude Code: write `autoMode` entries at user scope, since the classifier ignores `autoMode` in project and local settings.
- Codex: join the entries into `auto_review.extra_policy`, then validate with `codex features list`. `render.rad` restores the previous file when validation fails; tai should too.
- OpenCode: skip with a warning.
- Ownership of entries works as it does for hooks.

From reading the code: config assets install through `installConfigAsset` (`internal/install/installer.go`), with each adapter declaring what it supports (`SettingsKey` in `internal/adapter/claude/claude.go`, `SupportedConfigAssetTypes` in `internal/adapter/codex/codex.go`, which lists only hooks and MCP). tai rewrites Codex's `config.toml` by reparsing and re-rendering it, which drops comments and key order; that is why `ConfigWriteConsent` asks first. `render.rad` edits the file preserving comments, so moving the policy into tai either costs that or needs a comment-preserving TOML edit. Codex's policy is a single string built from many entries, so per-entry ownership means tai has to recognize the paragraphs it wrote inside that string.

The settings-fields asset (card `support-settings`) is the same gap for `enabledPlugins`, `env` and `defaultMode`, which the same repos fill with a merge script and a jq step. Both write owned entries into a target's settings, so they should share that machinery rather than grow two copies.

Done when the auto-approval bundle installs its policy with no `render.rad` and no `post_install` step.

(Moved from GitHub issue #13, part 1.)
title: Add an approval-policy config asset (Claude auto mode, Codex auto-review)
